title: Amemiya 2019 · Seated pseudo-walking and trunk PPS
citation: Amemiya, T. (2019). Creating a Walking Sensation for the Seated—A Sensation of Pseudo-walking Expands Peripersonal Space. NTT Technical Review, 17(11), 23–27.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

published_method.source_scope: Technical feature summarizing one underlying assessment, with no independent cohort established by the feature.
published_method.sound: Frontally approaching headphone white noise simulated by sound-level variation.
published_method.heel_conditions: Compare bilateral playback of recorded footsteps low-pass filtered at 120 Hz, asynchronous playback with randomized step onsets, and 60 Hz sinusoidal vibration at step onsets. Average amplitude is matched across active conditions.
published_method.chest_target: A suprathreshold 150 Hz sinusoidal chest vibration, delivered by a pendant voice-coil in the Japanese companion. Detect it quickly with a button press.
published_method.reference: English Figure 3 describes a no-vibration reference. Japanese Figure 3 describes an absent auditory-stimulus condition. The records do not establish which cue or cues the comparison omitted.

stimulus_type.value: Looming white noise, chest target vibration and heel conditioning
